1. This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Govt. vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

sentences.text: The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi, was acquired.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the recorded owner/bhumidhar in possession of full share in the land bearing Khasra no. 48/1 min (400) total admeasuring 4 Bigha 00 biswas situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5. It is stated that the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.
The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioner as the physical possession of the land has not been taken and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioner.

The LAC passed the award in a mechanical way without applying the mind and without going through the LAC no. 395/2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Murti Devi v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 claim filed by the petitioner, as such the award is not acceptable to the petitioner, and she has received the awarded amount under protest and without prejudice to their rights.

entities.text: Murti Devi v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC failed to take note of the actual and practical market value of the said land and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.
The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value adjudicated by the courts.
The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

6. It is stated that the said land is well connected with the transport, telecommunication, roads and have all the basic amenities in and around the surrounding areas i.e. Mundka railway station is 1.5 kms away from the said land, Mundka Udyog Vihar Extension is located at a distance of about 2.5 kms away from the said land, where commercial activities are carried out and reputed clubs and party lawns are located within a radius of 24 kms away from the said land; godown of Food Corporation of India is at a distance of 3.5 kms away from the said land, District Sports School and the bottling plant of Indian Oil Corporation and Fortunes World's biggest 500 companies are at a distance of 3.5 - 4 kms away from the said land, NH10 is at a distance of 2 kms away from the said land and Azad Hind Gram is at a distance of 4  5 kms away from the said land.
LAC no. 395/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Murti Devi v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 7.

8.

sentences.text: It is stated that the situation of the above stated areas shows the great importance in assessing the market value of the said land, and the similarly situated land was sold @ Rs. 2000/ per square yards by the vendors, therefore, the said land, which could easily fetch the same rate and the said land cannot be granted the market value less than Rs. 2000/ per sq. yards.
As such the ld. LAC has failed to take note of the judicial pronouncements and the government policy of 10% yearly escalation in the market value of the said land.

9. It is stated that the respondent no.2 has allotted the adjoining Rohini residential land to persons for residential as well as commercial purposes for more than Rs. 6000/ per square yards and that too, only to those who has applied for the plots/flats and shops well in advance, which fact shows that that the land for residential and commercial purposes was LAC no. 395/2016 (Award No.

sentences.text: The respondent no.2 has been allotting the plots at the remotest and undeveloped the land, therefore, it is clear that the respondent no.2 cannot gain/earn profit at the cost of causing loss to the petitioner.
10. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money.
The ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioner.

The ld.
LAC has grossly erred in directing the deduction of tax, from the amount of compensation of the said land as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.
It is stated that the petitioner has claimed the compensation for the acquire land @ Rs.2000/ per square yards in addition to Rs. 25,000/ per bigha, solatium amount along with interest.

11. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/Union of India and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation as the ld. LAC while passing the Award has taken into consideration all legal requirements and material on record and has rightly assessed the correct market value of the said land on the date od the notification under Section 4 of the Act.
All the averments made in the petition were denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.
LAC no. 395/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Murti Devi v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 11 12.

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the said land has been taken over by the DDA and as per Kabza karwahi report dated 29.11.2007 the said land has been taken back by the L&B department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.
It is also written in Kabza Karwahi that the compensation/alternative allotment/enhanced compensation will be paid by DSIDC.
It is submitted that as the DDA is not the beneficiary of the said land, therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation.
It is prayed that the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?

OPP 2. Relief.
14.

Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence.
Counsel for the petitioner as well as ld.

16. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLE D FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
OPP 17.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
18.

sentences.text: Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

21. In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 2005 06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ram Kishan (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).

This court adjudicate the market value of land of the LAC no.
395/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Murti Devi v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 11 petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.

sentences.text: 22. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 23.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).

(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
LAC no. 395/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Murti Devi v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 11 24.
